targets.label: Game-used football jerseys
targets.note: Football scope — matcher should require game-used/game-worn language (lectr's guUseClass: never used↔issued) and treat photo-matched as the A-grade anchor. Corpus depth here is real: 38K+ game-used sold lots.

targets.label: Philadelphia Eagles sports cards
targets.note: Team-scoped hunt over a player-keyed book: identify() still resolves each listing to its cardKey (player|year|set|#|grade) for pricing — the Eagles filter is the discovery lens (Hurts/Barkley/McNabb/Reggie White/Chuck Bednarik era all qualify). Card-vertical entry rides the hunt budget, not the cards cap.

targets.label: Charles Schulz — signed material
targets.note: Format-aware (autographFormatOf): a Schulz ALS/TLS vs signed book vs signed print are different markets — never cross-comp. PSA/DNA-certified pieces anchor risk grade A.

targets.label: Charles Schulz — original sketch / drawing
targets.note: Original Peanuts art (Snoopy/Charlie Brown sketches, strip art). Separate entry from signed-material on purpose — originals are the art market, signatures are the autograph market. Fairly-priced originals are rare enough that the looser 0.15 bar applies.

targets.label: Vintage Apple / early computing
targets.note: Rides the culture→science reroute (science-tech): Apple-1/II era hardware, Jobs-signed material, early manuals/business cards. lectr's TECH regexes (rr-auction.ts) transfer to identify(). Beware modern-refurb noise — require pre-1998 signals or signed provenance.

targets.label: Maurice Sendak — signed material
targets.note: Signed Wild Things firsts and later editions dominate; format gate applies (signed book ≠ signed print ≠ ALS).

targets.label: Maurice Sendak — original sketch / drawing
targets.note: Original ink/watercolor pieces — same originals-vs-signatures split as Schulz. Wild Things character sketches are the grail class.

targets.label: Fossils — corpus-comparable classes
targets.note: Scope to the classes the corpus actually prices (885 sold fossil lots, gates just fixed for naturals): dinosaur teeth (T-rex/raptor), ammonites, trilobites, megalodon. eBay's raw "fossil" firehose is mostly $10 decorative — matcher should require genus/species or slab-style language and lean on size context. Expect "hunted — no book value" labels until the fossil book rows deepen.
